newsitem.title: USA: Lam Research sees lower sales ahead.
newsitem.headline: Lam Research sees lower sales ahead.

text.p: Lam Research Corp said in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing that revenue levels in the remaining quarters of fiscal 1997 may be lower than in the first quarter of 1997.

"The company anticipates that its sales will continue to be adversely affected by this (semiconductor) slowdown and therefore the revenue levels achieved for the remaining quarters of fiscal 1997 may be lower than the revenue levels achieved in the first quarter of fiscal 1997," the company said in a 10Q filed on November 13.
The company reported net sales of $276.2 million in the first quarter.
The company also said in the filing it expects the current semiconductor slowdown to continue to adversely impact its operating results through fiscal 1997.
It also said that there is no assurance the company will be able to remain profitable in the future.

The company also said it expects royalty income will decrease in subsequent quarters as the current royalty agreement with Tokyo Electron Limited which was due to expire in December 1996, has been renewed at a significantly lower royalty rate.

In August, Lam Research announced it would cut 11 percent of its workforce as part of a restructuring. It said about 310 regular and 240 contract positions have been eliminated, and that it will take a pretax restructuring charge in the first quarter of $11 million to $12 million, or $0.25 to $0.28 per share, fully diluted.
